directions.S: SOUTH, facing the viewer squarely, front view
directions.SE: SOUTH-EAST, front three-quarter view facing screen-right
directions.NE: NORTH-EAST, rear three-quarter view facing away toward screen-right
directions.N: NORTH, full back view facing away, no face visible
directions.NW: NORTH-WEST, rear three-quarter view facing away toward screen-left
directions.SW: SOUTH-WEST, front three-quarter view facing screen-left

phases: 0: exact relaxed idle, right hand holding sword down beside body, matching direction reference
1: left hand joins same hilt, draw the weapon slightly forward near waist, knees soften subtly
2: begin lifting the gripped sword along the dominant-side shoulder, blade rises above that shoulder without cutting across the face
3: both hands clasp the same hilt together directly above head, blade axis STRAIGHT VERTICALLY UP, crossguard above top fist, no leaning to screen-right
4: peak overhead anticipation, BOTH hands stacked over crown, sword remains STRAIGHT VERTICALLY UP, elbows naturally flexed and connected
5: start forceful downward cut, shoulders and elbows drive the hilt forward from overhead, blade begins its coherent forward-down arc
6: fast mid-downstroke, both hands retain one rigid grip, hips/torso engage, blade follows actual wrist rather than floating; keep head and limb dimensions unchanged
7: impact of decisive two-handed down-forward chop, weight shifts toward facing direction and knees bend slightly; sword points forward-down along facing vector
8: low follow-through continuous from impact, both hands hold hilt before lower torso, sword extends forward/down along facing direction
9: begin recovering the sword by bending elbows, torso settles from lunge, same clear hilt grasp
10: settle back toward the relaxed original stance, guide sword down beside dominant hand, release support hand naturally
11: exact original relaxed idle as phase0, same head, torso, feet and sword-carrying pose
